name: Contact mask aligner
purpose: Align and expose resist-coated wafers; ideal for conventional neural-electrode masks.
geometryBrief: Separate lamp housing, microscope arms, split-field views, wafer chuck, mask frame, XY/theta controls, CRT/control panel and base.
behaviorBrief: Model loading, focus, alignment error, contact/proximity mode, exposure and resist image. Lock one documented configuration before tracing panels.
inputs: Coated wafer revision, mask transmission map, two alignment marks, XYθ pose and exposure mode
outputs: Latent-image map, registered mask transform and overlay residuals for development
acceptance: Apply a known translation to two separated alignment crosses. The measured overlay must reproduce the offset, then vanish to raster precision after inverse alignment.

name: Manual mask aligner
purpose: Rapid contact lithography on small wafers or coupons.
geometryBrief: Benchtop frame, binocular optics, substrate stage, mask clamp and mechanical knobs.
behaviorBrief: Reusable aligner engine with model-specific stage travel and mask fit.
inputs: Coupon and chuck envelopes, mask geometry, alignment marks and requested stage pose
outputs: Mask-to-coupon transform, latent image and stage-limit result
acceptance: Fit a coupon to the selected chuck, then request a position beyond the documented travel. The valid pose exposes the intended field; the second request preserves the incoming coupon.
geometryStatus: Reference-informed physical-scale GLB; enclosure and strokes estimated
simulationStatus: Ideal hard-contact dose and overlay; eight analytic/contract test bodies passed
integrationStatus: Dedicated simulator; revision and dose-map export; browser CI configured
related: SUSS MJB3 operator manual, Feb 1984 rev A

name: Maskless laser writer
purpose: Directly expose patterns without a physical mask.
geometryBrief: Enclosed tool, loading hatch, sample stage, workstation and status lights.
behaviorBrief: Import layout; simulate write-field stitching, dose and overlay, not proprietary control code.
inputs: Vector pattern, write-field grid, sampling pitch, stage offsets and resist revision
outputs: Stitched exposure map with field coordinates and dose provenance
acceptance: Write a line across two virtual fields. Zero offset joins the line continuously; a programmed lateral offset appears only at the seam to within one pixel.
geometryStatus: Reference-informed metric glTF; internal dimensions inferred
simulationStatus: Two-stripe commanded dose model; analytic acceptance checks passed
integrationStatus: Simulator route and exposure-revision export; local Chromium QA passed; production verification pending

name: Photomask pattern generator
purpose: Write photomasks for repeatable multilayer processes.
geometryBrief: Tall enclosed cabinet, motion system and operator terminal.
behaviorBrief: Mask geometry, write resolution and alignment marks; separate from wafer processing.
inputs: Mask blank ID, artwork, write grid, fiducials and polarity
outputs: Mask revision with writable-area bounds, feature map and fiducial coordinates
acceptance: Write asymmetric fiducials on a mask blank and load it into the aligner. Its orientation and tone must survive the handoff, and the original wafer must remain untouched.

name: Electron-beam lithography
purpose: Fabricate nanoscale test structures and dense contact patterns.
geometryBrief: Column, chamber, load lock, vacuum cabinet and operator display.
behaviorBrief: Pattern dose/blur and proximity-effect approximation; chamber state and write progress.
inputs: Resist grid, vector shapes, beam-dose map and declared blur kernels
outputs: Deposited-dose image, threshold contour and estimated write duration
acceptance: Place two isolated identical point features. With a normalized linear kernel, their combined dose must equal the sum of the isolated responses and conserve integrated input dose on a padded grid.
integrationStatus: Simulator route and sample revision export

name: Optical projection stepper
purpose: Repeat a reticle pattern across a wafer.
geometryBrief: Large cabinet, reticle handling and wafer loader; use sectional schematic for hidden optical path.
behaviorBrief: Field stepping and overlay; do not invent precise lens prescription.
inputs: Reticle artwork, projection scale, wafer outline, die pitch and field poses
outputs: Per-field exposure map, incomplete-field flags and overlay records
acceptance: Step an asymmetric reticle over a 2 × 3 grid wholly within a wafer. Count six copies, spaced by the configured pitch, with feature size set by the declared projection scale.

name: Spin coater
purpose: Apply resist or polymer films to substrates.
geometryBrief: Lid hinge, bowl, vacuum chuck, speed control, drain and dispensing pipette.
behaviorBrief: Film thickness vs calibrated speed curve, edge bead, substrate centering and recipe history.
inputs: Wafer outline and ID, resist ID, spin history and material-specific thickness calibration
outputs: Resist-layer revision with thickness map, centering record and calibration ID
acceptance: Reserve one measured spin-curve point during fitting. Predict its central film thickness and compare with the held-out reading and its predeclared uncertainty.

name: Coat/bake system
purpose: Integrate controlled spin coating and hotplate baking.
geometryBrief: Separate bowl and flat heated plate, lids, display and sample carrier.
behaviorBrief: Track coating and thermal history independently.
inputs: Substrate, coating calibration and two scheduled coating/bake operations
outputs: Resist revision with separate coating map and temperature-time record
acceptance: Run the same coat twice with different bake schedules. Pre-bake thickness maps must match; the two histories must show their respective bake traces.

name: Vapor prime oven
purpose: Prepare surfaces for adhesion before coating.
geometryBrief: Cabinet door, chamber rack, gauge and status panel; exact variant unresolved.
behaviorBrief: Surface preparation state and adhesion parameter; abstract chemistry.
inputs: Substrate surface ID, initial preparation state and compatible primer model
outputs: Surface-preparation event and material-specific adhesion state or unknown flag
acceptance: Process one of two identical virtual coupons. Only that coupon acquires the primer event; a material lacking adhesion calibration must return an unknown response.

name: Automated resist developer
purpose: Develop patterned resist in a controlled process.
geometryBrief: Enclosure, wafer handling, dispense assembly, monitor and reservoirs.
behaviorBrief: Convert latent image into mask openings using a calibrated development model.
inputs: Latent dose image, resist tone, initial thickness and dissolution model
outputs: Remaining resist-thickness map and open-region polygons
acceptance: Use a two-level exposure checkerboard and an ideal positive-tone threshold. Above-threshold squares must open and below-threshold squares must retain their film.

name: Automated coater
purpose: Repeat coat operations across wafer batches.
geometryBrief: Cassette slots, transport arms, dispense bowl and panel.
behaviorBrief: Batch queue, film thickness map and wafer tracking.
inputs: Cassette slot map, independent wafer IDs, coating jobs and film calibration
outputs: Per-wafer coat revisions, slot history and thickness maps
acceptance: Load three distinguishable wafers and cancel the middle job. Only the two completed IDs receive films; every output must resolve to its original slot.

name: Inspection microscope
model: Nikon Eclipse LV100 / LV100ND (choose exact variant)
purpose: Inspect patterned features, alignment and visible defects.
geometryBrief: Stand, nosepiece, objective turret, stage, eyepieces and illumination controls.
behaviorBrief: Optical inspection scene with scale bar, focus and defects from fabrication state.
inputs: Patterned sample, reflectance image, stage transform, objective profile and focal plane
outputs: Calibrated inspection image with defect coordinates and scale bar
acceptance: Measure a known line-pair pitch in a virtual stage micrometer at two objective settings. Pixel spacing must change with magnification, while physical pitch agrees to within one image pixel.
